title: Add hose-clamp-barb task by eainx · Pull Request #1892 · robocurve/benchmark-tasks · GitHub
comments: Push a coolant hose onto a barbed pump outlet and tighten its worm-drive clamp with a nut driver Connect the hose to the pump's outlet and clamp it. Fitting a hose to a barbed spigot and clamping it is routine work for auto mechanics and general maintenance and repair workers (coolant, fuel, air and water lines). The hose has to be pushed past the barb's bead all the way to the shoulder, or it blows off under pressure, with the worm-drive clamp's band on the barb behind the bead, and the clamp driven tight with a nut driver: turned, let go and re-gripped as a hand does, while the socket stays seated on the small screw head. Action allowance: 1,600 steps (80 seconds at 20 Hz) Recorded results: Dream-1 run: 0 after 129 steps (6.45 simulated seconds); termination: DreamSessionExpired:expired. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 795 steps. Reproduction: task README, task-specific scene/scorer, and exported runtime with pinned Docker build recipe. Media: M-Q49LJL (Dream recording, setup screenshot, and full-score demo when needed). Simulation fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. The hose is a rigid tube; the bead is drawn only, the barb's collider a slimmer pin. Pushed on lined up, the hose grips the barb by a slide joint (holding it on the barb's axis) with ~3 N drag, sprung against coming off once home. The clamp is held on the hose by a stiff joint. Screw turns come from the seated socket's measured twist: 0.4 turn snug, 0.8 tight, about three half-turns of the wrist; no reaction torque on the driver.
